text:
maria (sales): Quick sync: Simon at MeridianBank wants a POC for split-key BYOK. Requirements: split key material across two customer HSMs, monthly rotation, 2-hour maintenance window for any key ceremony, and full attestation logs. Can we map options?
ajay (solutions): We can support but with constraints. We don’t provide built-in Shamir threshold inside the runtime. Typical approaches: (1) customer performs split/unify outside Redwood and supplies wrapped DEKs, or (2) customer-run orchestration that performs per-request unwrapping and passes a short-lived token to Redwood. Both require customer orchestration for the multi-custodian flow.
ajay (solutions): Note operational tradeoffs: if both HSMs are required per-decrypt, performance depends on slowest KMS/hsm call. If customer is ok with our key-proxy holding a non-exportable CMK in their HSM (we never export key material), latency is much lower.
tori (crypto-ops): Compliance notes: we support CloudHSM and customer HSM via key-proxy. We can collect attestation artifacts (certificate chain, HSM firmware/hash, FIPS statements). The split-key ceremony itself is customer-run; we can plug into their process and record timestamps and usage logs.
micah (eng): Perf notes: unwrap-on-each-request with no caching will increase p95 by ~40-120ms depending on region/KMS RTT and adds KMS call costs. We can offer short-lived DEK cache (configurable TTL) to reduce KMS calls (example: 30s). If customer requires zero-KEK-exposure for runtime, we can do a hybrid: client-side unwrap to generate a session token we accept for a TTL.
simon (customer): Clarify: we require Redwood to never hold raw KEK material and guarantee that key components remain split. Is client-side unwrap and token exchange acceptable?
ajay (solutions): Yes. Option 1: you keep KEK parts and do assemble+unwrap inside your KMS, then call Redwood with a timebound token for DEK usage. Option 2: run Redwood inside your VPC/Private deployment and use our key-proxy to attach a CMK hosted in your HSM; Redwood will perform decrypts but cannot export key material. Both maintain zero-knowledge to different degrees.
tori (crypto-ops): Rotation: we can automate rotation triggers but multi-custodian ceremonies must be synchronized. For the POC we recommend a dry-run rotation step in staging to validate rollback and key-version compatibility. We also support DEK versioning so older tokens remain decryptable for a configured retention window.
claire (legal): Contract note: if Meridian insists on a 2-hour maintenance window for rotation, the SOW must define responsibilities and rollback criteria. Any manual steps done by Redwood or our engineers should be scoped and billed in the SOW (we typically estimate 8-24 eng hours for a multi-custodian dry-run). Also add a DPA clause for escrow and legal release processes if they want key escrow.
maria (sales): Pricing implications: per-KMS call fees + our proxy overhead. For unwrap-on-each-request expect incremental cost approximate $0.02-$0.08 per decrypt depending on cloud KMS pricing, plus increased latency. We'll include detailed line items in the quote.
simon (customer): We need an actual SOW and a test plan with success criteria before committing to Dedicated. Also a sample runbook for a rotation ceremony.
ajay (solutions): Proposed POC outline: 1) 10-day sandbox with staging HSMs; 2) two modes: strict (unwrap-per-request) and cached (DEK TTL = 30s); 3) workload: 50-100 TPS spike, run perf for p50/p95 latency, KMS-call counts, error/fallback tests; 4) deliverables: attestation artifacts, rotation dry-run report, runbook, and cost appendix. Acceptance: sustain 80 TPS with p95 <200ms in cached mode and successful rotation dry-run with no data loss.
micah (eng): Staging config example we can ship: 
```
redwood.deploy:
  key_management:
    mode: envelope_cache
    dek_cache_ttl_ms: 30000
    kms_endpoints: ["meridian-staging-hsm-a","meridian-staging-hsm-b"]
    unwrap_on_request: false
```
(For strict mode set unwrap_on_request: true and dek_cache_ttl_ms: 0.)
ajay (solutions): Action items: I will draft the SOW + test plan by tomorrow EOD. Micah to prepare staging config + perf harness. Tori to enumerate required attestation artifacts and minimum KMS APIs we’ll call. Claire to prepare contract language variants (no-escrow, escrow, role of legal process for release). Maria to prepare cost appendix.
simon (customer): Thanks — please include an explicit statement about not storing raw KEK material in the SOW. Well review and schedule kickoff after SOW review.
maria (sales): Ack. We'll circulate early draft today. :thumbsup:
